correctness.rationale: For integers \(a,b\ge2\), write \(c=3a+2b\) and \(K=2^{a-1}3^{b-2}\). Then \(D(2^a3^b)=3Kc\), \(D(\varphi(2^a3^b))=K(c-2)\), and \(\varphi(D(2^a3^b))=Kc\prod_{q\mid c,q\ge5}(1-1/q)\), where the product ranges over distinct prime divisors. Hence commutation requires an Euler-product deficit of exactly \(2\). Any prime \(q\ge5\) dividing \(c\) forces \(c/q\le2\); the possibility \(c=q\) yields deficit \(1\), whereas \(c=2q\) yields deficit \(2\). Thus \(a=2u\) and \(3u+b\) prime, with converse. Dirichlet proves the fixed-\(b\) infinitude dichotomy. The exact count is \(\sum_u(\pi(X+u)-\pi(3u+1))\), giving \(C(X)\sim X^2/(4\log X)\) by the uniform prime number theorem. The checker independently verified 2916 exponent pairs and comparison to the OEIS entry through 2048.

value.rationale: OEIS A260961 poses a natural arithmetic-function commutation problem but supplies enumeration only. The first nontrivial two-prime-support multiplicative semigroup, restricted to its natural interior where both small primes divide the relevant derivative values, admits a complete prime-parametric classification with a fixed-exponent infinitude dichotomy and the asymptotic \(X^2/(4\log X)\). The exact intrinsic exponent-height asymptotic provides structural information rather than an unmotivated finite slice; the unrestricted problem remains open.
